Given data:
- Weight of block 1 ($W_1$) = $50\text{ kN} = 50,000\text{ N}$
- Weight of block 2 ($W_2$) = $40\text{ kN} = 40,000\text{ N}$
- Inclination of plane $\theta = 30^{\circ}$
- Coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.10$

For the system to move to the right, both blocks tend to move up the inclined plane, and the hanging weight $W$ moves downwards.

**1. Equilibrium of Block 2 ($40\text{ kN}$):**
Let $T_1$ be the tension in the string between block 1 and block 2.
$$T_1 = W_2 \sin\theta + \mu W_2 \cos\theta$$
$$T_1 = 40000 \sin(30^{\circ}) + 0.10 \times 40000 \cos(30^{\circ})$$
$$T_1 = 40000(0.5) + 4000(0.866) = 20000 + 3464 = 23,464\text{ N}$|

**2. Equilibrium of Block 1 ($50\text{ kN}$):**
Let $T_2$ be the tension in the string passing over the pulley to weight $W$.
$$T_2 = T_1 + W_1 \sin\theta + \mu W_1 \cos\theta$$
$$T_2 = 23464 + 50000 \sin(30^{\circ}) + 0.10 \times 50000 \cos(30^{\circ})$$
$$T_2 = 23464 + 25000 + 4330 = 52,794\text{ N}$$

**3. Required Weight $W$:**
Since the pulley is frictionless, the weight $W$ balances the tension $T_2$:
$$W = T_2 = 52,794\text{ N} \approx 52.79\text{ kN}$$
proTip: When blocks move upwards along an incline, the frictional force acts downwards parallel to the plane, opposing the motion.
